title: In Ezekiel 40 In What Ways Does The Return Of Gods Glory To The Temple Impact Our Understanding Of Gods Presence In Our Lives
paragraphs: The Return of God's Glory to the Temple in Ezekiel 40: Understanding God's Presence in Our Lives

Ezekiel 40 begins an extraordinary vision of a future temple, given to the prophet during Israel's exile. This vision spans several chapters, culminating in the dramatic return of the glory of the Lord to the temple (see Ezekiel 43:1-5 ASV). By exploring these passages, we gain profound insight into the nature of God's presence—not just for ancient Israel, but for believers today.
The Context: Exile and Hope

Israel’s exile in Babylon was marked by a deep sense of loss, especially after the departure of God’s glory from Solomon’s temple (Ezekiel 10:18-19 ASV). The vision in Ezekiel 40-48 offered hope: a promise of restoration, holiness, and renewed relationship. The temple symbolized God’s dwelling among His people.
The Return of God’s Glory
In Ezekiel 43:2 ASV, Ezekiel describes the return of the glory of God:
And, behold, the glory of the God of Israel came from the way of the east: and his voice was like the sound of many waters; and the earth shined with his glory. - Ezekiel 43:2 ASV

This event marks the reversal of God’s departure. The vivid imagery—a radiant, overwhelming presence—signals restoration and hope. God’s glory fills the temple, declaring that He has chosen to dwell again among His people.
Implications for Understanding God’s Presence
1. God’s Desire to Dwell with His People

From Eden to the wilderness tabernacle, from Solomon’s temple to the vision in Ezekiel, Scripture consistently presents a God who desires to be present with His people (Leviticus 26:11-12 ASV). The return of the glory in Ezekiel underlines His commitment, even after judgment and exile.
2. The Holiness of God’s Presence
The careful measurements and detailed ordinances in Ezekiel 40-42 emphasize God’s holiness. His glory could only return to a purified, consecrated temple:
And he said unto me, Son of man, this is the place of my throne, and the place of the soles of my feet, where I will dwell in the midst of the children of Israel for ever. - Ezekiel 43:7 ASV
God’s presence is not casual; it is holy and transformative.
3. Anticipation of Christ: The True Manifestation of God’s Presence
The New Testament reveals that Jesus is the ultimate fulfillment of God’s presence with humanity. John declares:
And the Word became flesh, and dwelt among us (and we beheld his glory, glory as of the only begotten from the Father), full of grace and truth. - John 1:14 ASV
Jesus is the true temple (John 2:19 ASV), and through Him, believers experience God’s glory and presence directly.
4. The Indwelling of the Holy Spirit
For believers today, God’s presence is not limited to a physical building. Through faith in Christ, the Holy Spirit dwells within us:
Know ye not that ye are a temple of God, and that the Spirit of God dwelleth in you? - 1 Corinthians 3:16 ASV
The return of God’s glory to the temple in Ezekiel foreshadows the greater reality that, in Christ, God is present with, and within, His people.
5. The Promise of Future Glory
Ezekiel’s vision finds its ultimate fulfillment in the new creation, when God’s presence will be fully realized:

And I heard a great voice out of the throne saying, Behold, the tabernacle of God is with men, and he shall dwell with them, and they shall be his peoples, and God himself shall be with them, and be their God. - Revelation 21:3 ASV
The story of God’s glory returning to the temple points to the hope of eternal communion with God.
Conclusion

The vision of God’s glory returning to the temple in Ezekiel 40-43 is a rich tapestry that shapes our understanding of God’s presence: He is both transcendent and immanent, holy and merciful, just and gracious. For believers, this vision points to the reality of Christ’s work and the indwelling Spirit, assuring us that, though the world changes, God’s desire to dwell with His people endures forever.
